formula: Who are you to + base verb + other information?

formulas.formula: Who are you to + base verb + other information?

example: Who am I to judge someone else’s lifestyle?
exampleZh: 我有甚麼資格批評別人的生活方式？

examples.en: Who am I to judge someone else’s lifestyle?
examples.zh: 我有甚麼資格批評別人的生活方式？
examples.highlight: Who am I to judge someone else’s lifestyle?

rules.zh: 在 Who am I to...? 或 Who are you to...? 句式中，to 後面必須接動詞原形；不可使用現在分詞或過去式。
rules.en: Use the base verb after “to” Who am I to judge them? Who am I to judging them? Who am I to judged them?

rules.zh: 主語 I 必須配合 am，寫成 Who am I to...?；主語 you 必須配合 are，寫成 Who are you to...?，兩者不可互換。
rules.en: Use “am” with I and “are” with you Who am I to...? Who are you to...? Who are I to...? Who am you to...?

rules.zh: 這個句型通常不是真的要求對方回答，而是表達：自己沒有資格批評別人；自己不應干涉別人的選擇；對方沒有權利命令或批評自己；對方沒有足夠知識或經驗作出判斷。
rules.en: It is normally a rhetorical question

rules.zh: 通常表示謙遜、自我反省或克制。我有甚麼資格告訴她應該選擇甚麼職業？ 通常用來直接挑戰對方，語氣可以非常強烈。你有甚麼資格閱讀我的私人訊息？ 在工作、正式場合或與陌生人交談時，使用 Who are you to...? 可能顯得無禮或帶有敵意。
rules.en: “Who am I to...?” and “Who are you to...?” have different tones Who am I to...? Who am I to tell her what career to choose? Who are you to...? Who are you to read my private messages?

rules.zh: 自然的核心語序是：【Who + am/are + subject + to + base verb...?】 這個固定反問句本身通常位於問題開首。真正自然的句式變化來自：在前面加入語氣詞；在中間加入插入語；在後面加入 when、if 或 because 類資料；把整個問題放進直接引語；在動詞後接名詞、that 子句、whether 子句或 wh-子句。不應為了製造表面變化而把核心字詞移到不自然的位置。
rules.en: The core expression has a fairly fixed order Who + am/are + subject + to + base verb...?

rules.zh: 這句通常表示：我有甚麼理由不接受這項提議？或我當然應該接受。它與本課的「我沒有資格做某事」意思不同，因此不包括在本練習內。
rules.en: Do not confuse it with “Who am I not to...?” Who am I not to accept the offer?

benefits.zh: 目標表達【Who am I to...?】可以表示你知道自己的知識、經驗或立場有限，因此不會隨便批評別人。它能把自我反省和原因自然地放在同一句中。
benefits.en: It helps you show humility Who am I to...? Instead of: I should not judge her because I do not know her situation. You can say: Who am I to judge her when I do not know her situation?

benefits.zh: 目標表達【Who are you to...?】可以直接質疑某人是否有權命令、批評、控制或干涉別人。你有甚麼資格決定我應該怎樣花自己的錢？ 這比單純說 I disagree with you 更清楚地指出問題在於對方沒有權力作出該決定。
benefits.en: It helps you challenge unfair interference directly Who are you to...? Who are you to decide how I should spend my money?

benefits.zh: 這個句型可以把「我沒有足夠資格、權力或知識」濃縮成一個簡潔自然的反問句。
benefits.en: It shortens a longer explanation Instead of: I do not have enough knowledge or authority to question the doctor’s advice. You can say: Who am I to question the doctor’s advice?

benefits.zh: 這個句型經常出現在日常對話、電影對白、爭論和內心獨白中。與較平淡的敘述句相比，直接反問能更清楚地表達人物的情緒和態度。
benefits.en: It can make dialogue more realistic She asked, “Who are you to accuse me?”

benefits.zh: 使用不同形式，可以表達不同程度的語氣：謙遜、反思承認自己的限制不滿、質疑強烈挑戰掌握這些變化，可以令說話和寫作中的人物態度更加清楚。
benefits.en: It helps you control your tone Who am I to...?: After all, who am I to...?: Really, who are you to...?: Who are you, exactly, to...?:

benefits.zh: 這個核心句型可以：單獨使用；配合開首語；加入插入語；接 when 或 if 子句；放入直接引語；接 that、whether、what、how 等子句。因此，學生不需要把所有答案機械地寫成完全相同的形式。

questions.answerZh: 我提醒自己：「我也會犯錯，有甚麼資格要求別人做到完美？」
questions.highlight: I reminded myself, “Who am I to expect perfection from other people when I make mistakes too?”

questions.prompt: The chairperson asked the speaker what right he had to dismiss an idea before the committee had discussed it.

questions.prompt: I have no right to assume that silence means agreement.

questions.prompt: When I saw evidence that contradicted my view, I realised that I had no right to ignore the facts merely because they were inconvenient.
questions.promptZh: 當我看到與自己觀點相反的證據時，我明白自己不能只因為事實令人不便便忽視它們。
questions.answer: When I saw evidence that contradicted my view, I thought, “Who am I to ignore the facts simply because they are inconvenient?”
